title: Good Apples in a Bad Barrel
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Drawing on decades of research, including Philip Zimbardo's work, this piece explains how even highly positive, empathetic team members can be pulled toward negativity when surrounded by disgruntled colleagues. It argues this happens not because good team members are gullible, but because their empathy makes them listen more attentively to complaints than they should. The article calls on leaders to move quickly to address bitter, negative team members before their influence spreads through the team. It closes with a stark recommendation: when a negative team member can't let go of their distaste, they need to be removed.
points: Positive, empathetic team members are especially susceptible to being pulled negative by disgruntled peers.
This happens because their empathy makes them listen closely to complaints, not because they're gullible.
Zimbardo's research is cited as evidence that people conform to peer social influence even against their own experience.
Leaders must move swiftly to address the root cause with a negative team member before the attitude spreads.
When a negative team member can't surrender their distaste for the organization, removal is the recommended step.
quotes: Research over decades has confirmed that good apples placed in a bad barrel will turn sour.
Their positive qualities of fairness, empathy, objectivity and compassion encourage them to listen more attentively than perhaps they should.

More than 50 years ago, Stanford professor Philip Zimbardo proved in a series of controversial experiments that people are likely to conform to the social influence of peers even when their viewpoints go against their personal experience.
But when one or more team members go negative and lodge complaints and criticisms to negatively influence others, leaders must act swiftly to curtail the virus that is likely to spread.
Waiting and hoping for the best is how good teams turn sour.
